requirements.requirement: The system must reuse the existing regex matching pipeline in specialty_service.py to identify exact specialty matches between user input and NUCC taxonomy.
The system must reuse the existing vector expansion pipeline to generate semantically related specialty terms from user input.
The system must classify matches into exact, partial, or inferred categories based on regex and vector outputs.
The system must assign a higher score weight to exact matches than partial matches.
The system must assign a higher score weight to partial matches than inferred matches.
The system must compute a normalized specialty match score between 0 and 1 inclusive.
The system must aggregate multiple matched NUCC taxonomy codes into a single composite score.
The system must produce deterministic scores for identical inputs and provider taxonomy data.
The system must return a score of 1.0 when an exact specialty match is found with no ambiguity.
The system must return a score of 0 when no regex or vector matches are found.
The system must handle multiple user-requested specialties by evaluating each and combining results into a single score.
The system must prioritize higher-confidence matches when multiple match types are present.
The system must use vector similarity thresholds to determine inferred relevance matches.
The system must ensure inferred matches do not exceed the score contribution of partial matches.
The system must log intermediate match classifications (exact, partial, inferred) for downstream explainability.
The system must handle empty or null user specialty input by returning a score of 0 without error.
The system must handle providers with missing or empty NUCC taxonomy data by returning a score of 0.
The system must avoid duplicate counting of the same NUCC code across regex and vector pipelines.
The system must support case-insensitive and normalized text comparison for specialty matching.
The system must produce scoring outputs compatible with the schema defined in EVAL-SPC-001.
